title: Non-invasive assessment of cutaneous sodium concentration by 23Na MRI in homeostatic and inflammatory skin conditions
summary: The skin can store sodium. Previous research suggests that the amount of sodium in the skin may change in inflammatory skin diseases. This study investigates the amount of sodium in the skin of people with atopic dermatitis or psoriasis and whether it differs from that of healthy individuals. The study also examines whether sodium levels differ between affected and less affected skin areas and whether they change during the course of treatment. A special type of magnetic resonance imaging is used to measure sodium in the skin without an invasive procedure. In addition, skin structure, disease activity and superficial skin samples are examined. Participation in the study does not alter the patients' medical treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults aged ≥18 years who are capable of providing informed consent and have sufficient German language proficiency to independently understand the written study information and informed consent procedure. Eligible participants include patients with a confirmed diagnosis of atopic dermatitis or psoriasis vulgaris receiving outpatient or inpatient care at the Department of Dermatology, University Hospital Düsseldorf, as well as healthy controls without known chronic inflammatory skin disease and without acute inflammatory skin disease of the lower legs. Participants must be able to safely undergo the planned MRI examination.
Exclusion criteria:
Contraindications or other conditions preventing the safe performance of MRI, particularly claustrophobia, artificial heart valves, implanted electrical devices (e.g. cardiac pacemakers or cochlear implants), non-permitted metallic implants or foreign bodies, intrauterine contraceptive devices, implanted drug pumps, and pregnancy. Participants with relevant hearing disorders, tinnitus or increased sensitivity to loud noises, acute or chronic diseases substantially affecting their general condition or making MRI an additional burden, or advanced severe organ disease are also excluded. Further exclusion criteria comprise relevant intolerance to MRI-related auxiliary materials, inability to provide informed consent, insufficient German language proficiency, and lack of consent to be informed about medically relevant incidental findings. Persons in a direct employment, training or examination-related relationship of dependency with the study team are also excluded.
